title: Atlas cross-field link
description: One edge of the cross-field causality map, in atlas/crosslinks/<fieldA>__<fieldB>__<slug>.yaml. Physicist's four-part record (a/b patterns, connection, label, breaks_if) plus two tags: support (mechanism | mathematics | analogy) and claim (cause | pattern). verify/validate.py adds: claim=cause needs support=mechanism and at least one cited, verified source id; support=analogy needs label ANALOGY-ONLY and claim=pattern; every cited id must exist in sources/.

pattern.description: The pattern as it appears in this field, in that field's own terms.

refs.description: Optional atlas ids this side points at: an atlas link (l.*), a meaning (prr.*), or a card (c.*).

connection.description: The mechanism, shared mathematics, or published result that connects a and b. For an analogy, say plainly that there is none.

support.description: mechanism: one causal process acts in both fields. mathematics: different systems obey the same equations or universality class. analogy: resemblance only.

claim.description: cause: something in a produces or constrains something in b. pattern: a and b share form; neither causes the other.

breaks_if.description: The observation that would break this link.

analogy.description: Hesse (1966) analogy table. Required when support=analogy.

steps.description: Optional per-step chain from a to b. Each step carries its own label. verify/validate.py enforces that the link's overall label is no stronger than its weakest step (a chain is only as certain as its least certain step).

support.description: Optional. If absent, the step inherits the link's support. Under claim=cause every step must be mechanism.

evidence_rung.description: Strength of causal evidence about the REAL system (Pearl's ladder, Pearl & Mackenzie 2018): 0 = none (analogy only), 1 = seen together (association/pattern), 2 = shown by intervention (experiment or natural experiment with exogenous timing), 3 = counterfactual: a causal model made a locked prediction about the real system before the data were opened, and it held. A simulation alone never raises the rung; it sets model_exists.

model_exists.description: True if a formal or simulation model of the mechanism exists (cite it in model_refs). Says nothing about the real system.

rung_basis.description: Required for rung >= 2: what intervention, natural experiment, or locked prediction earns the rung.

locked_prediction.description: Required for rung 3: the source that made the prediction before the data, and the source that confirmed it.
